subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Breaking the Sound Barrier
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Breaking the Sound Barrier.

hook.text: On October 14, 1947, Chuck Yeager flew the Bell X-1 past Mach 1. He broke the sound barrier with two cracked ribs.

buildup.text: As planes approached Mach 1, violent shaking — called buffeting — made control nearly impossible. Several test pilots died trying.

discovery.text: Shock waves form when air can't move aside fast enough. These waves compress air into walls of intense pressure.

twist.text: The X-1 used a moveable horizontal stabilizer instead of elevators. This innovation maintained control through the transonic zone.

climax.text: The flight was classified for a year. When revealed, it opened the era of supersonic aviation and space exploration.

punchline.text: Cracked ribs. Mach 1. The barrier wasn't physical. It was an engineering problem.

quiz.question: What innovation allowed the Bell X-1 to maintain control through the sound barrier?
options: A specially designed cockpit that pressurized to counteract G-forces
A moveable horizontal stabilizer that replaced conventional elevators
Rocket engines that provided constant thrust regardless of air pressure
